title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Cloudflare
providers.scope_notes: Covers Cloudflare (API, Zero Trust Access, R2). All plans have API tokens and 18-month Audit Logs v2; Logpush beyond 18 months is Enterprise; Access service tokens need Cloudflare Zero Trust; R2 credentials need R2.

controls.name: Service Token Duration
controls.what: Sets the service token's expiration date.
controls.setting: Zero Trust > Access controls > Service credentials > Service Tokens

controls.name: Automatically clean up inactive service tokens
controls.what: Disables or deletes tokens unused for 30-365 days.
controls.setting: Zero Trust > Access controls > Access settings > Manage service tokens

controls.name: Strict service token authentication
controls.what: Only Service Auth policies authorize token requests, no session cookie is issued, and failures are logged.
controls.setting: Zero Trust > Access controls > Access settings; strict_service_token_auth

controls.name: Disable / delete service token
controls.what: Disable stops authentication; delete revokes for good.
controls.setting: Service Tokens > Disable token / Delete; DELETE .../access/service_tokens/{id}

controls.name: Rotate service token secret
controls.what: Issues a new secret with an optional grace period for the old one.

no_control.what: Revoking existing Access sessions does not stop a valid service token; only deletion does.

controls_unknown: Any account-level setting to block members from creating user API tokens or using the Global API Key.
Any account-wide policy forcing token expiry or IP filters.
Whether Super Administrators can list or revoke other members' user API tokens.
Whether dashboard SSO or Access policies are checked on API token / Global API Key requests (no explicit statement).
Exact Audit Logs v2 action names for token create/delete/roll.
Whether Origin CA keys still authenticate after the 2026-09-30 removal date.
IP restrictions for Access service tokens and for R2 S3 requests.
Cloudflare OAuth tokens (actor context 'oauth', e.g. Wrangler) were not researched.

authentication.summary: Client ID + Client Secret (cfast_ prefix for new secrets) sent as CF-Access-Client-Id/CF-Access-Client-Secret headers to reach apps protected by Cloudflare Access.

federation.details: Service Auth policies authorize the token without an IdP login.

ip_restriction.boundary: Add an IP ranges Require rule to the Service Auth policy of each Access application; IP ranges are checked at login and continuously. Not a property of the token itself.

lifetime.summary: Duration chosen at creation; optional auto-disable/delete after 30-365 days of inactivity

renewal.expiry_basis: Duration from creation; Refresh adds one year
renewal.summary: Refresh or edit duration; rotate secret with a 1 hour to 30 day grace period.

administration.summary: Admins can disable, delete, rotate and auto-clean tokens; strict service token mode (forced on for orgs created on/after 2026-10-05) stops cookie issuance and logs failures.

sso.details: Service tokens are used with Service Auth policies, which do not require an IdP login.

offboard.details: Service tokens are account-level credentials for automated systems, not tied to a user.

inventory.details: Zero Trust > Access controls > Service credentials > Service Tokens; API: GET /{accounts_or_zones}/{account_or_zone_id}/access/service_tokens.

network.ui: Zero Trust > Access controls > Policies > (Service Auth policy) > add Require rule, selector 'IP ranges'

usage.api: POST /client/v4/graphql, dataset accessLoginRequestsAdaptiveGroups, filter on serviceTokenId

reads.api: Enterprise HTTP request logs via Logpush (filter ClientRequestHost/ClientRequestURI for the app)

token_format.notes: Secret cfast_ + 40 chars + 8-char checksum (since 2026-08-26); Client ID ends .access; older secrets are 64-char hex.

log_sources.name: Access authentication logs
log_sources.notes: Failed requests for recognized tokens logged in strict mode.

log_sources.name: Audit Logs v2
log_sources.notes: Admin changes to service tokens (create/rotate/delete) via API.

credential_id_fields.notes: Docs say the name identifies events in logs; exact field name not given

anomaly_cues: Token used on apps it is not authorized for

containment.steps: Delete the service token (DELETE .../access/service_tokens/{id}); disabling also stops the old secret during a rotation grace period.
containment.notes: Revoking Access sessions alone is not enough.

calls.call: HTTP request to an Access-protected application path (customer app)
calls.log_notes: Per-request logs need Enterprise HTTP request logs/Logpush; Access authentication logs record only the authentication, not app actions.

unknown: Calls depend on the protected application
